overall: Atlanta saw a strong warm-up through the afternoon, with temperatures peaking at 91.4°F (the running max) around 16:19 ET — notably above what NWP models had forecast. Since then, a line of severe thunderstorms (including active Tornado Warnings and Severe Thunderstorm Warnings from NWS Peachtree City) has caused a dramatic 9°F temperature collapse, with the 17:52 observation back down to 80.6°F and cooling rapidly at -4.5°F/hr. The active severe weather environment is the dominant story for the remainder of the evening.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models underforecast the daily high by meaningful margins: ECMWF=87.5°F, NBM=86.8°F, and even the warmest model HRRR=89.6°F all came in below the observed running max of 91.4°F. The INTRADAY model's 96.8% probability in the 90-91°F bucket was closest to correct, and the META model's distribution straddling 90-91°F and 92-93°F (31.6% each) brackets the actual result well.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is almost certainly already locked in at 91.4°F — the current running max recorded at approximately 16:19 ET. The give-up classifier fired at hour 14.67 when the running max was 89.6°F, correctly anticipating the peak was imminent. With severe thunderstorms ongoing, temperatures now at 80.6°F and falling at ~4.5°F/hr, and the NWS evening forecast calling for continued storms through 11 PM, there is virtually no path to additional warming tonight. Confidence is very high (>95%) that 91.4°F is the final TMAX.
